- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next period.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce volatility amplification.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 values (neutral or negative), model often underperforms; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for hidden risk.
